Who this trip suits

Choose the Situk if you want a named river salmon trip with a clear species and access plan. A bank session and the full float have different transport, effort and equipment needs. Discuss your ability on uneven ground and your comfort in moving water.

A guided float can suit someone who wants help with the route and fishing decisions, but confirm the time, boat access and ability to stop. Do not treat the full float as a short bank visit with a boat added.

When to go: separate sockeye and coho

ADF&G describes sockeye entering the Situk during June and July, with fish distribution moving upriver through the run. Its coho guidance emphasizes fresher fish in the lower river and notes that fish farther upstream can show spawning color later in September.

This does not establish a complete coho booking calendar. The agency page’s date widget contains malformed values, so this guide does not use it for exact dates. Ask the Yakutat area office and your operator about the species, run stage and reach for your intended week.

Check Southeast Alaska regulations and Yakutat emergency orders again close to the trip. A historical run window does not prove that a reach is open or a fishing method is permitted.

Source: ADF&G: Situk River sockeye and coho · ADF&G: sport fishing regulations · ADF&G: emergency orders and news

How to arrange the Yakutat day

ADF&G describes road access from Yakutat to Nine Mile Bridge and a separate road to Lower Landing. Choose the actual starting point, take-out and transport plan. Save both pins offline and agree who moves the vehicle.

For a float, confirm the expected duration, current river conditions, guide qualifications for the activity and the exit plan. For a bank visit, agree a turn-back time and suitable footwear. No water level or wading depth is declared safe by this article.

Source: ADF&G: Situk River sockeye and coho

What the guide provides: confirm shuttle and sizes

Request an inventory of boat equipment, rods, reels, terminal tackle, waders, boots and safety equipment. Ask who supplies and arranges the shuttle. A rod package does not imply footwear or transport.

Confirm drying access at your accommodation and baggage limits with each transport provider. If you intend to retain fish where permitted, ask separately about processing, storage and the trip home. No lodge package or operator availability is verified here.

Local mistakes to avoid

  • Booking “salmon season” without naming sockeye or coho.
  • Choosing the bank reach only because it is close to the road.
  • Failing to arrange the take-out and shuttle for the full float.
  • Using a general Alaska forecast as a river access decision.
  • Buying waders before confirming whether you will wade and what sizes the operator supplies.

Regulations and licenses

Use ADF&G’s sport license and regulations pages. Select the Southeast Alaska rules and the Situk/Yakutat area, then search emergency orders for the trip date.

Ask the operator to confirm the legal reach, target, method and any current restrictions. Fees, limits and rules can change. This guide links the authority instead of storing those details as permanent facts.

Source: ADF&G: fishing licenses · ADF&G: sport fishing regulations · ADF&G: emergency orders and news

Questions and answers

How long is the Situk River float?

ADF&G describes about 14 river miles from Nine Mile Bridge to Lower Landing. Ask the operator for a duration based on the current river and fishing plan.

When do sockeye enter the Situk?

ADF&G describes a June–July entry period. Confirm the current run, reach and emergency orders before you travel.

Do I need waders for a Situk trip?

That depends on the bank, float and wading plan. Ask about access, suitable footwear, sizes and confirmed rental or guide provision before buying.
